claim: The Seventh Circuit held that when Kmart's loss prevention officers, acting in coordinated detention with local police, subjected Wrenhollow to custodial interrogation on store premises, Miranda warnings were constitutionally required before any questioning could begin. The court reasoned that the degree of police involvement transformed the private detention into state action sufficient to trigger Fifth Amendment protections.
citation: Wrenhollow v. Kmart Corp., 748 F.2d 319 (7th Cir. 1984)
initial_reasoning: In Wrenhollow v. Kmart Corp., 748 F.2d 319 (7th Cir. 1984), the Seventh Circuit held that Kmart loss‑prevention officers, acting in concert with local police, created a custodial environment on private premises that required Miranda warnings before interrogation. The court reasoned that the police involvement transformed the private detention into state action, invoking Fifth Amendment protections.
